answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring each identity to forge a unique pigment seal%3A a computational commitment that binds a stable sable hardware fingerprint to an ephemeral opal challenge derived from the epoch beacon. Attackers must recompute the full seal for every fake identity because the pigment is non-transferable and the opal rotates unpredictably%2C so the marginal cost of a new sybil is a full proof-of-work solve rather than a cheap copy. Honest agents pay once per epoch for their single identity.
